title: Cack Riley, the lot where parades meet, and his baseball team
summary: Playing trombone and cornet with Cack, the nearby lot used for Mardi Gras parades, and the ball team he organized, the Cheeky Men.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I haven't seen Allen in years. Cack, probably Cack Riley. Cack Riley has pictures in that book.

I used to play with Cack once in a while, go home and get the cornet, when this boy used to have Lion of Laurel, it used to be George Stokes, they'd put a nickel in his lot in the March of the Bobcats. Cack would get his trombone, walked around, I'd go and get the trombone, they'd have a few beers you know.
The place is monsters now you're talking about.
That's right. But I only live two blocks from there.
We still go there every time.

Well I have to go down to Mardi Gras if I want to see somebody I know. And most of the Mardi Gras parades, the marching parades meet there. And I used to play ball in that lot, and have my own team in one town.
And you played ball and cornet at the same time?

No. The league was open and George talked, and George says, get us a band. We got a band like Bill Craig and a couple of other guys. We opened the day, put the trumpet down, ran the pitcher's box without warming up and start pitching. But we lost that day. And guess the name of my team, Jake? What? The cheeky man. The cheeky man?

The cheeky guy is supposed to be a nervy guy, you know. Cheeky. Let me your automobile, I want to go up to Baton Rouge. That's after you were married in 1938. Yeah, that was after around 1938. Well they had a real fine ball player named Bull Raw. I used to pitch for the Pelicans. He was sitting at the meet and he said, you can't use that name. I said, what's going to stop me? A little cheeky man. I think we were sabotaged.
Who made the sweatshirts for you?
We bought them and we stenciled them.
